name: navbar-two-row
title: Two-row navbar
description: A header in two rows: brand, search and account links on top, the categories underneath, scrolling sideways on a phone.
docs: Put the search field in search (a SearchTrigger, a form), the account, help and bag in utilities and the categories in categories; catalogue is the trailing link to everything. The header is sticky with a negative top, the height of the first row, so on scroll the first row slides away and only the categories stay: plain CSS, no scroll listener. While keyboard focus is inside the first row the whole bar unpins (CSS :has and :focus-visible), so a control you tab to is never out of sight above the window, and it pins again as soon as focus moves on. It counts on the first row's fixed height (56px on a phone, 48px more with the search row, 64px from md), so keep your mark within it, and it works when the header sits in the container that scrolls, the page or a layout of your own. Under md the search gets a row of its own and the categories are one scrolling line with fade edges and the current one brought into view. Mark the current page with currentHref, set sticky={false} to keep the bar in the flow, use linkAs for your router's Link and navLabel to name the categories landmark.
